classification.difficultyReason: Use the right-isosceles cross section to establish width 2h and the supplied volume target, then differentiate and convert the inflow units.

content.prompt: The water trough in the diagram is in the shape of an isosceles right triangular prism, 3 metres long. A farmer is filling the trough with a hose at the rate of 2 litres per second.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the volume of water in the trough when the depth is $h$ cm is $V=300h^2\text{ cm}^3$.

spec.description: Open triangular-prism trough, downward-pointing right-isosceles cross section, horizontal water surface, perpendicular depth h, right-angle marks, dashed hidden edges and longitudinal 3 m dimension. Source grey water shading becomes house light blue; unrelated face shading is omitted.
spec.mathematics: The cross section has a right angle at its bottom vertex. The perpendicular water depth is h; the water-surface width is not supplied as a label.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram givens remain visible in the question edition.

answer.worked:
The vertical depth bisects the right-isosceles cross section. Let $x$ cm be half the water-surface width. Then
$$\begin{aligned}\tan45^\circ&=\frac{x}{h}\\x&=h.\end{aligned}$$
The water-surface width is therefore $2h$ cm.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Cross-sectional area}&=\frac12\times2h\times h\\&=h^2\text{ cm}^2.\\V&=h^2\times300\\&=300h^2\text{ cm}^3.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given that 1 litre is $1000\text{ cm}^3$, find the rate at which the depth of the water is changing when $h=20\text{ cm}$.
